grh_7527e502df5fdf814e78.title: The Double Seven
paragraphs: Expansion of the Double Seven has brought rancher Git Baskin into a bitter dispute with neighboring homesteaders, and Baskin makes matters worse by hiring gunman Clint Sutton after cattle begin disappearing. Britt discovers that one of the farmers, Ruth, has deliberately been stealing cattle and stirring up violence because he wants Baskin to burn the settlers out. Years earlier another large rancher destroyed Ruth's Texas farm and his wife Nancy died in the fire, leaving him obsessed with recreating the conflict and taking revenge on any rancher who resembles his old enemy. Britt stops the plot, while Baskin agrees to drop the cattle grievance and get rid of Sutton.

Other credited names include Jack Johnstone as director, Frank Burt as writer, Hal Gibney as host, Lamont Johnson as announcer, and Hal Gibney as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. Characters credited in this version include [[character|Britt Ponset]].

grh_7546f4d1c5c9bad60de2.title: Orange Blossoms
paragraphs: Baron Roger Belmer can inherit a fortune only by satisfying a marriage condition in his aunt's will, so while engaged to Helen he enters a temporary marriage of convenience with Kitty that is supposed to end in divorce after a year. Living apart does not prevent Roger and Kitty from developing real feelings for each other. When Helen discovers that the arrangement has become personal, the financial scheme collapses.
